newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African near-term industrial futures took a whack at the start of trade on Wednesday and struggled to regain composure throughout the day, dragging industrial shares down with them.

Futures players attempted to buoy very frail industrial share futures contracts by shedding the stocks and snatching the futures. While avoiding a slide, industrial shares floundered throughout the day to finish weak.
South African futures were knocked after the U.S. December Standard and Poor futures index was battered overnight and dealers said the smack must have come from the Australian or Eastern markets.
The soft South African market failed to find support in Wall Street's slight hop overnight as panic arising from negative sentiment entrenched itself.
"The futures were very much down this morning, but Wall Street was up. Still we seemed to dismiss any gains on Wall Street and slid with the futures worry," a dealer said.
"Australian and Asian markets were knocking S&P futures and when they opened up a while ago they were still down," he said.
Dealers said that world markets would be nervously eyeing Wall Street's open which was seen lower.
By 1445 the Dow Jones industrial index had lost over one percent.
"There is some concern about how Wall Street will open up and it's likely industrials will be down again. It's all up to Wall Street now," a dealer said.
Gold shares on the other hand made a feeble start to the day as bullion slept, but as the metal price livened up to lift itself above $369 gold stocks inched up.
Overall, dealers said volumes were high.
The industrial index was 45.6 points off at 7,851.8, the all-shares lost 27.3 points to 6,639.1 and the golds inched up 15.4 points to 1,542.1.
Johnnic lost 125 cents to 52 rand, De Beers off 175 cents at 138 rand, Gencor shed 20 cents to 16.75 rand, Freegold added 60 cents to 35.85 rand and Amgold was steady at 380 rand.
Making a volatile start due to the S&P anxiety, industrial equity futures failed to regain lost ground and finished down.
The December industrial contract was much weaker at 7,457/68 from 7,621, the all gold was at 1,068/72 from 1,064 and the all-share was at 5,970/6,000 from 6,105.
